subject: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Asha �����������good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps around the access controls items you called out: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Data residency: FinTrust requires EU-only storage and processing for PII.
- RBAC: fine-grained roles (admin, auditor, app-user, data-ingest) and attribute-based scoping by tenant/team.
- Support access: support engineers may need ephemeral access for triage; break-glass must be auditable and require approval.
- Audit & retention: detailed access logs required, retention ~12-24 months (you mentioned 13 months).

What we can provide (high level):
- Region pinning: we can pin your account to our EU region (Frankfurt) and ensure all persistent storage and logs stay in-region.
- RBAC: role templates + custom roles; attribute scoping (org/team) is supported; we can share a starting RBAC matrix.
- Support & break-glass: ephemeral support sessions with short-lived credentials, mandatory justification, automated ticket approval flow, and full audit trail (who, when, duration, command-level logs where possible).
- Logs & retention: configurable audit log retention; we can retain detailed audit events for 13 months and provide exports.

Attachments: I’ve attached a brief RBAC diagram and a sample RBAC matrix for your review. Also attaching a SOC 2 summary for initial compliance context.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the retention window you need for audit logs (you mentioned 13 months)?
2) Would you like a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Neha) to validate the break-glass workflow and logging schema?
3) Please share any internal RACI or required roles if you want us to map them to our role templates.

Proposed time for a 30-45m deep-dive: Thu 11/19 10:00-11:00 CET or Fri 11/20 09:00-10:00 CET. I’ll hold both tentative slots.

Thanks - Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

- redwood_rbac_diagram.png (900KB image stub)
- rbac_matrix.csv (spreadsheet stub)
- SOC2_summary.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Asha Mehta <asha@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming retention: we need audit logs retained for 13 months minimum (EU residency).
- RBAC: we’ll map the FinTrust roles to your templates, but we also need attribute-based scoping for "team_id" and "environment" (prod/staging).
- Support access: break-glass must include an approval step from our security on-call (SMS + email), and we need immutable evidence of the approval + session transcript/command log where available.

Jordan and I are available for the deep-dive. Fri 11/20 09:00-09:45 CET works for us.

Also attaching our internal RACI for reference.

Best,
Asha
Asha Mehta
Head of Security, FinTrust
asha@fintrust.com

Attachment: FinTrust_RACI.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@fintrust.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Hi Asha - appreciate the details. A few technical notes to address the items you listed:

1) EU residency and retention:
- We can pin your account to the eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) cluster. All persistent storage (model artifacts, customer data, audit logs) will be provisioned in-region.
- Audit logs: we support configurable retention policies; we can set 13 months by default for your account and provide daily exports to an S3-compatible endpoint you control if desired.

2) RBAC & attribute scoping:
- Role model: support for built-in roles (owner, admin, developer, auditor) and custom roles.
- Attribute-based access: we support resource tags and claims (e.g., team_id, environment). Policies can be authored in our policy language and scoped by those attributes.
- I’ve attached a starter RBAC matrix that maps common FinTrust roles to our templates - please mark where you need changes.

3) Support access & break-glass:
- Support sessions use short-lived, just-in-time credentials provisioned via our access broker.
- Break-glass workflow: requires a PagerDuty/On-Call approval (we can integrate with your on-call via webhook); approval is stored with the session metadata.
- For audit evidence we capture: approver identity, timestamp, justification, session start/end, and an optional command transcript when the affected surface supports it. Transcripts are stored encrypted in-region and tied to the session record.

4) Logging schema and exports:
- Audit events include actor, action, resource, request metadata (IP, user-agent), and request/response hashes.
- We can provide JSON line exports or push events to a customer-owned collector.

If that aligns, I’ll prepare a short technical pack (policy examples, retention config, webhook doc) before the Fri deep-dive.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: rbac_matrix.csv (csv stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Thanks Asha - sounds good and aligned. Confirming next steps: 

1) We’ll set account-level retention to 13 months and pin the account to eu-west-1. Rachel will share the technical pack (policy examples + webhook integration) by EOD Thu.
2) Neha will run the deep-dive on Fri 11/20 09:00 CET (technical invite to follow) - purpose: validate break-glass flow and audit exports.
3) FinTrust to mark up the attached RBAC matrix with specific role mappings; we’ll iterate and produce a final mapping for contract annex.

I’ll create the HubSpot deal record and add the artifacts and meeting notes. If anything urgent comes up before the call, ping me directly.

Best - Marissa
